objectClass.notes: Static monumental landmark building, exterior shell only. No interior geometry: a prop kit is only ever looked at from outside, so an interior costs draw calls, geometries and VRAM for something nobody sees. Nothing moves, so one root pivot and zero sockets is the correct contract. A long low hall whose front is an open colonnade and whose back is a solid wall, sheltering a 15 m gilded Buddha lying on its right side facing the colonnade, head propped on its right hand, left arm draped to the thigh and the legs stacked. A three-step stone terrace runs the whole length in front of the columns and steps out on +X as a forward apron; seven square columns and a wall-pier at the head end carry a shallow two-tier HIPPED roof in terracotta fish-scale tile with an ochre border course, grey capped hip ribs and a long ridge; the figure lies on a low two-step plinth with its soles turned down the length of the hall.

reasoning: The registry notes make an argument rather than a description: the figure is modelled as part of THIS asset and the long front is an open colonnade, because the two decisions depend on each other. A closed long low box has no recognisable feature at all and reads as a warehouse.
So this is a building AND a large statue, and its material budget has to cover both gold leaf and roofing. The figure is the only ORGANIC form in the whole kit.

Occlusion risk is the HIGHEST of the batch and scored 3: the identity of the prop is a figure seen THROUGH a colonnade, so every column is a chance to hide it, and the figure is reviewed from a straight-on side elevation as well as from the hero angle.
Material layers scored 3 in the third build: four post-construction multiplier tiles (stone grime, tile courses, gilt tarnish, smoke staining) sit over five textureless materials.
Action readiness is minimal: static landmark geometry, box collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The figure cannot be a box decomposition and cannot be a lathe. It is a long soft mass whose section changes at every point along it -- shoulder to waist to hip to calf -- which needs a station-by-station tube, and that is a shape helper written for this asset alone.

resolvedUnknowns: The rear elevation is a solid wall: the plate shows it solid at both corners and the proxy reconstructs it solid. Whether the real building is colonnaded on both long sides cannot be known from one view.

The head end's front corner is a 2.5 m wall-pier, read off a 2x zoom of the plate (scratch/_bud/front_zoom.png): a white slab from the front corner back, with the end colonnade's column visible behind it. The feet end is open with one mid column.

The figure's robe folds, the incised hairline, the facial features and the 108 auspicious marks on the soles are NOT authored. The figure carries its posture, its proportion, its ushnisha and its toe comb -- what reads through a colonnade at prop distance -- and nothing finer.

The figure is authored at 15.9 m head to toe with its body top at 4.2 m, half the column height, which is where the plate puts it; the second build's 3.3 m body top was a figure lying too small in its own hall.

The interior is a solid mass with a dark face, not a room. This prop is an exterior shell even though its interior is what you look at -- what you look at is the FIGURE, and behind the figure a single dark panel does the work of a room.
The roof tiles are individually laid fish-scale tiles in the plate with a three-course ochre border; the model carries them as ONE seamless course tile at 0.17 m courses in running bond.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 12.38 x 10.00 x 19.24 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=32000 triangles, <=24 draw calls, <=16 materials, <=32 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot and zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

pivotInventory.name: root
pivotInventory.justification: The ONLY mechanism this prop has. Static landmark geometry: nothing opens, turns or swings, so every part is fixed and gets no axis. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on it.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.

colliderInventory.note: Declared on the asset as box. One convex proxy over the whole envelope; a level builder collides with the hall, not with the figure inside it. coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center as the asset declares, +Y up, long axis on Z, colonnade facing +X. The figure lies on its RIGHT side facing the colonnade, which puts its head at +Z and its feet at -Z (body up = right x forward = (-Y) x (+X) = +Z), so from the front the head is at the viewer's left as it is on the plate, in the bay beside the head-end wall-pier. The hall is NOT centred in x: it occupies the -X side of the platform and the forward apron takes the rest, which is why the roof is centred at x=-2.10 rather than on the origin.

silhouette.description: A long stepped terrace, a colonnade from 1.50 to 6.95 m, and a shallow two-tier hip roof to a ridge at 9.99 m. The prop is nearly twice as long as it is tall, and the silhouette events are the column rhythm, the two roof steps with their hips, the long ridge, and the forward apron breaking the platform outline on one side. The figure is not in the silhouette at all: it is seen only THROUGH the colonnade. Against the proxy the band table reads mean |delta width| 0.025 and |delta depth| 0.027 of height (second build 0.074 / 0.079); the one band over 0.05 is band 1, where the proxy fuses the terrace top into a 10.5 x 17.8 m slab.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x spans -6.19..+6.19, set by the bottom platform slab (the hall on -X, the forward apron on +X); z spans -9.62..+9.62, set by the lower tier's flared eaves ring (authored 9.62/1.045 so that hipRoof's own 4.5% eaves flare lands exactly on the envelope); y spans 0.00 to 9.99, the ridge cap over an upper-tier apex at 9.80. The envelope itself was re-declared from 14 x 10 x 28 in the second build, from two agreeing proxies (trellis 1.852, hunyuan 2.020 length/height against the first build's 2.818), and the third build re-cut every element inside it from the proxy's own orthographic elevations (scratch/_bud/side.png, end.png at 55.2 and 83.4 px/m): columns 1.50 to 6.95, hall 7.2 m deep in plan, ridge 0.70 of the eaves length, upper eaves 0.89 of it.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Meshy's image-to-3d refuses this plate with content_policy_violation (the safety checker is forced on at the endpoint), so the proxy is fal-ai/trellis with fal-ai/hunyuan3d/v2 as a second opinion -- two independent reconstructions that agree to 8.7% on length/height. The trellis mesh is the reference.glb the band table and the depth-map elevations are read from.

viewEvidence.note: NOT OBSERVED. The plate shows the colonnade elevation and the feet end; the proxy's back is a solid wall and its far (head) end carries a solid panel, both consistent with the plate's visible corners, so the blank back wall is the reading with the best evidence rather than a guess.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.91, up from 0.86. The second build had the right envelope and the right roof FORM; what it lacked was read off the proxy's own elevations and a 2x zoom of the plate: a taller colonnade (5.45 m against 4.85), a narrower and longer hall (band table 0.074 / 0.079 -> 0.025 / 0.027), a 13.5 m ridge, a wall-pier at the head end with seven columns instead of a twelve-column peristyle, a figure a quarter larger in section on a low plinth, and the wear that is this plate's identity at prop distance -- black column feet, scalloped courses, tarnished gilt, a smoke-stained interior -- as four post-construction canvases over five textureless materials. Remaining drag is the figure's unauthored surface (robe folds, face, soles) and lightingCamera 0.84 on a plate whose subject is in shade. 3,244/32,000 triangles, 8/24 draw calls, 5/16 materials, 8/32 unique geometries, 4 canvases at 5.3 MB, factory ~70 ms.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the hero4x class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Seven components and one repetition system: 8 of 24, the lightest draw-call load of the monumental set. The stone material alone serves the platform, the plinth, the wall and pier, the nine columns and the hip ribs.

materials.note: stone covers five consumers; five materials of sixteen, eleven in hand. The four wear canvases add no material: each is bound to an existing one as map and bump after construction.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 3,244 of 32,000 -- still the lightest prop in the batch. The figure is about 2,400 triangles at 32 segments, and it is the whole identity of the asset. The headroom is deliberate: the plate shows the figure only through columns and in shade, which is thin evidence for finer work.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: A station-by-station tube, two hipped cones per tier and boxes. The tube is the only organic form in the kit and was written for this asset alone.
One InstancedMesh system carries 9 of the prop's 30 discrete parts. Every instance is checked separately by check-coplanar, so one soffit at the wrong height reports as nine pairs.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Every material is declared textureless as a sculpt material; four Canvas 2D multiplier tiles (512 px, ~70 ms, 5.3 MB) are bound after construction: stone grime phase-locked to the column base, fish-scale courses on the tile and band, gilt tarnish, smoke on the interior. Under Node there is no canvas and every material keeps its flat colour. The figure's robe folds and the 108 auspicious marks on its soles remain unauthored.

risks.description: Meshy refuses the plate (content_policy_violation, safety checker forced on), so the proxy is trellis with hunyuan as a second opinion.
risks.mitigation: Two independent reconstructions agree to 8.7% on length/height and 3.2% on width/height; the band table against trellis reads mean 0.025 / 0.027 of height on this build. The proxy fuses the terrace top into one slab (band 1 at -0.10), which is a proxy artefact and left as the plate shows it.

risks.description: The clean gilt ships at #BA824A under a tarnish tile against a measured #AC8E6F brightest-quartile albedo.
risks.mitigation: The figure is the one surface in the plate that is never directly lit, so its measured chroma is a shade reading; the tarnish tile takes the tiled surface back to the second build's #AC7741 value where the patches are. The whole chain -- mean #7D6040, quartile #AC8E6F, shipped #AC7741 then #BA824A under tarnish -- is recorded on the material.

risks.description: Robe folds, hairline, facial features and the sole markings are absent.
risks.mitigation: The figure carries posture, proportion, ushnisha, toe comb and tarnish -- what reads through a colonnade at prop distance.
